verses.1:1: And the word of the Lord came to Micah the son of Morasthi in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, concerning what he saw regarding Samaria and regarding Jerusalem.
verses.1:2: Hear words, peoples, and let the earth pay attention, and all who are in it; and the Lord, the Lord will be among you as a witness, the Lord from His holy house.
verses.1:3: For look, the Lord is coming out from His place, and He will come down upon the high places of the earth,
verses.1:4: and the mountains will be shaken beneath Him, and the valleys will melt like wax before fire, and like water rushing down a slope.
verses.1:5: All these things are because of the ungodliness of Jacob, and because of the sin of the house of Israel. What is the ungodliness of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what is the sin of the house of Judah? Is it not Jerusalem?
verses.1:6: And I will make Samaria into a fruit-watcher's hut of a field and into a planting of a vineyard; and I will pull down her stones into a chasm, and I will uncover her foundations.
verses.1:7: And they will cut to pieces all her carved images, and they will burn all her wages in fire, and I will make all her idols into a desolation; for from the wages of prostitution she gathered them, and from the wages of prostitution she collected them.
verses.1:8: Because of this she will wail and lament, she will go barefoot and naked; she will make a wailing like that of dragons and mourning like that of daughters of sirens,
verses.1:9: for her wound has prevailed, because it has come as far as Judah and has reached as far as the gate of My people, as far as Jerusalem.
verses.1:10: You who are in Gath, do not exalt yourselves; you who are in Akim, do not rebuild mockery from a house; sprinkle earth upon your mockery.
verses.1:11: She who inhabits her cities well, she who inhabits Sennaar, did not go out to wail for the house next to her; she will receive from you a wound of pain.
verses.1:12: Who began toward good things for her who inhabits pains? Because evils came down from the Lord upon the gates of Jerusalem,
verses.1:13: a sound of chariots and horsemen. She who inhabits Lachish, she is the originator of sin for the daughter of Zion, for in you Israel's acts of ungodliness were found.
verses.1:14: Therefore she will give those who are sent away as far as the inheritance of Gath, vain houses; they came to nothing for the kings of Israel,
verses.1:15: until they bring the heirs, you who inhabit Lachish; an inheritance will come as far as Adullam, the glory of the daughter of Israel.
verses.1:16: Shave yourself and cut your hair for your delicate children; enlarge your widowhood like an eagle, for they have been taken captive away from you.
verses.2:1: They came to be devising troubles and working evil things on their beds, and at daybreak they carried them out, because they did not lift up their hands to God.
verses.2:2: And they coveted fields, and they plundered orphans, and they oppressed houses, and they plundered a man and his house, and a man and his inheritance.
verses.2:3: Therefore thus says the Lord: "Look, I am devising evils against this tribe, from which you will by no means lift up your necks, and you will by no means walk upright suddenly, for it is an evil time."
verses.2:4: In that day a proverb will be taken up against you, and a lament will be lamented in melody, saying, "We have suffered utter misery; the portion of my people has been measured out with a cord, and there was no one to hinder him from turning away; our fields have been divided up."
verses.2:5: Therefore you will have no one casting a cord by lot in the assembly of the Lord.
verses.2:6: Do not weep with tears, nor let them shed tears over these things; for he will not ward off reproaches,
verses.2:7: the one who says, "The house of Jacob has provoked the Spirit of the Lord." Are these His practices? Are not His words good with him, and have they walked uprightly?
verses.2:8: And formerly My people stood up in enmity; opposite his peace they stripped off his skin, so as to take away hope, a crushing of war.
verses.2:9: The leaders of My people will be cast out from the houses of their luxury; because of their wicked practices they were driven out. Draw near to everlasting mountains.
verses.2:10: Rise and go, for this is not rest for you because of uncleanness. You have been destroyed with destruction,
verses.2:11: you have been pursued with no one pursuing; a spirit set up falsehood, it dripped to you for wine and strong drink. And it will come about from the drop of this people,
verses.2:12: Jacob will surely be gathered with all; I will surely receive the remnant of Israel, together I will set his return; like sheep in distress, like a flock in the midst of their resting place, they will leap out from among people.
verses.2:13: Through the breach before them they broke through, and they passed through a gate and went out through it; and their king went out before them, and the Lord will lead them.
verses.3:1: And he will say, "Listen now to these things, rulers of the house of Jacob and remnant of the house of Israel. Is it not for you to know justice?
verses.3:2: You who hate good things and seek wicked things, tearing their skin off them and their flesh off their bones.
verses.3:3: Just as they devoured the flesh of my people, and stripped their skin off them, and crushed their bones and cut them in pieces like flesh for a cauldron and like meat for a pot,
verses.3:4: so they will cry out to the Lord, and He will not listen to them; and He will turn His face away from them at that time, because they acted wickedly in their practices against them."
verses.3:5: Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who lead My people astray, who bite with their teeth and proclaim peace upon him, and when nothing was given into their mouth, they raised up war against him:
verses.3:6: "Therefore there will be night for you without vision, and there will be darkness for you without divination; and the sun will set upon the prophets, and the day will grow dark over them.
verses.3:7: And those who see dreams will be put to shame, and the diviners will be mocked, and all of them will speak against them, for there will be no one who listens to them."
verses.3:8: Unless I fill up strength by the Spirit of the Lord and of justice and might, to declare to Jacob his acts of ungodliness and to Israel his sins.
verses.3:9: Listen now to these things, leaders of the house of Jacob and remnant of the house of Israel, who detest justice and distort all upright things,
verses.3:10: who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustices.
verses.3:11: Her leaders judged for gifts, and her priests gave answers for wages, and her prophets practiced divination for silver; and they leaned upon the Lord, saying, "Is not the Lord among us? Evils will by no means come upon us."
verses.3:12: Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem will be like a fruit-watcher's hut, and the mountain of the house will become a forest grove.
verses.4:1: And it will be in the last days that the mountain of the Lord will be visible, ready on the summits of the mountains, and it will be lifted up above the hills; and peoples will hasten to it,
verses.4:2: and many nations will go and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob; and they will show us His way, and we will walk in His paths." For from Zion law will go out, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem,
verses.4:3: and He will judge between many peoples, and He will rebuke strong nations even far away; and they will hammer their swords into plows and their spears into sickles, and nation will no longer raise a sword against nation, and they will no longer learn to wage war;
verses.4:4: and each one will rest beneath his vine, and each one beneath his fig tree, and there will be no one causing fear, because the mouth of the Lord Almighty has spoken these things.
verses.4:5: For all the peoples will walk, each one his own way, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and beyond.
verses.4:6: "In that day," says the Lord, "I will gather her who has been crushed, and I will receive her who has been driven out, and those whom I cast off;
verses.4:7: and I will make her who has been crushed into a remnant, and her who has been cast off into a mighty nation, and the Lord will reign over them on Mount Zion from now and forever."
verses.4:8: And you, gloomy tower of the flock, daughter of Zion, to you it will come, and the first dominion will enter, a kingdom from Babylon to the daughter of Jerusalem.
verses.4:9: And now why have you known evils? Was there not a king for you? Or has your counsel perished, that birth pains have seized you like a woman giving birth?
verses.4:10: Be in labor and be courageous and draw near, daughter of Zion, like a woman giving birth; because now you will go out from the city and camp in the plain, and you will come as far as Babylon; from there the Lord your God will deliver you from the hand of your enemies.
verses.4:11: And now many nations have been gathered together against you, saying, "We will gloat, and our eyes will look upon Zion."
verses.4:12: Yet they did not know the thought of the Lord, and they did not understand His counsel, for He has gathered them like sheaves of a threshing floor.
verses.4:13: Arise and thresh them, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horns iron, and I will make your hooves bronze; and you will melt down many peoples, and you will dedicate their multitude to the Lord, and their strength to the Lord of all the earth.
verses.4:14: Now the daughter will be hedged in with a hedge; he has set a siege against you; with a rod they will strike the gates of Israel on the cheek.
verses.5:1: And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, are very small to be among the thousands of Judah, from whom He will go out for Me to be a ruler of Israel, and His goings out are from the beginning, from days of old.
verses.5:2: Therefore He will give them up until the time of her who is giving birth; she will give birth, and the rest of their brothers will return to the sons of Israel.
verses.5:3: And He will stand and see, and the Lord will shepherd His flock in strength, and in the glory of the name of the Lord their God they will exist; because now He will be magnified to the ends of the earth.
verses.5:4: And this will be peace: when Assyria comes upon your land and when it treads upon your country, then seven shepherds and eight bites of men will be raised up against it;
verses.5:5: and they will shepherd Assyria with a sword and the land of Nimrod in its trench; and He will deliver from Assyria when it comes upon your land and when it treads upon your borders.
verses.5:6: And the remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like dew falling from the Lord and like lambs upon grass, so that no one may be gathered together nor stand firm among the sons of men.
verses.5:7: And the remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among beasts in the forest and like a young lion among flocks of sheep, just as when it passes through and separates and seizes, and there is no one who rescues.
verses.5:8: Your hand will be lifted up against those who afflict you, and all your enemies will be utterly destroyed.
verses.5:9: "And it will be in the day," says the Lord, "I will utterly destroy the horses from your midst and destroy your chariots,
verses.5:10: and I will utterly destroy the cities of your land and I will remove all your strongholds,
verses.5:11: and I will utterly destroy your sorceries from your hands, and diviners will not be in you;
verses.5:12: and I will utterly destroy your carved images and your pillars from your midst, and you will no longer bow down to the works of your hands,
verses.5:13: and I will cut down the groves from your midst, and I will wipe out your cities,
verses.5:14: and I will execute vengeance in anger and in wrath among the nations, because they did not listen."
verses.6:1: Hear now a word. The Lord, the Lord has said, "Arise, plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice."
verses.6:2: Hear, peoples, the judgment of the Lord, and you ravines, foundations of the earth, for the Lord has a judgment against His people, and with Israel He will enter into dispute.
verses.6:3: My people, what have I done to you, or how have I grieved you, or how have I troubled you? Answer Me.
verses.6:4: Because I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and from the house of slavery I redeemed you, and I sent forth before your face Moses and Aaron and Miriam.
verses.6:5: My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab planned against you, and what Balaam son of Beor answered him, from the reeds as far as Gilgal, so that the righteousness of the Lord may be known.
verses.6:6: With what shall I reach the Lord, lay hold of my God Most High? Shall I reach Him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
verses.6:7: Will the Lord be pleased with thousands of rams, or with ten thousands of fat torrents? Shall I give my firstborn for ungodliness, the fruit of my womb for the sin of my soul?
verses.6:8: Has it been told to you, man, what is good? Or what does the Lord seek from you except to do justice, and to love mercy, and to be ready to walk with the Lord your God?
verses.6:9: The voice of the Lord will be called out to the city, and He will save those who fear His name. Hear, tribe, and who will adorn the city?
verses.6:10: Is there fire, and a house of a lawless one treasuring up lawless treasures, and with arrogance, injustice?
verses.6:11: Will a lawless one be justified with a scale, and weights of deceit in a bag?
verses.6:12: From which they filled their wealth with ungodliness, and those who dwell in it were speaking lies, and their tongue, be lifted up in their mouth.
verses.6:13: And I will begin to strike you; I will wipe you out in your sins.
verses.6:14: You will eat and will not be filled, and it will grow dark in you and turn aside, and you will not be saved, and as many as are saved will be handed over to a sword;
verses.6:15: you will sow and will not reap; you will press the olive and will not anoint yourself with oil, and wine, and you will not drink; and the ordinances of My people will be wiped out.
verses.6:16: And you kept the statutes of Zimri and all the works of the house of Ahab, and you walked in their ways, so that I may hand you over to desolation and those who dwell in it to hissing, and you will bear the reproaches of peoples.
verses.7:1: Woe to me, for I have become like one gathering straw at harvest and like gleanings at the vintage, when there is no cluster to eat the first-grown fruits. Woe to me, soul,
verses.7:2: for a devout person has perished from the earth, and there is no one among people who acts uprightly. All of them go to law for bloodshed; each one oppresses his neighbor with oppression.
verses.7:3: They prepare their hands for evil. The ruler asks, and the judge spoke peaceful words; it is the desire of his soul. And I will take away their goods
verses.7:4: like a moth eating away and walking on a measuring rod on a day of watching. Woe, woe, your punishments have come; now will be their weeping.
verses.7:5: Do not trust in friends, and do not hope in leaders; guard yourself from her who shares your bed, so as not to confide anything to her,
verses.7:6: because a son dishonors a father, a daughter will rise up against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are all those in his house.
verses.7:7: But I will look to the Lord; I will wait patiently for God my Savior; my God will listen to me.
verses.7:8: Do not gloat over me, my enemy, because I have fallen, yet I will rise; for if I sit in the darkness, the Lord will give light to me.
verses.7:9: I will bear the wrath of the Lord because I have sinned against Him, until He vindicates my cause; and He will execute judgment for me, and You will bring me out into the light; I will see His righteousness.
verses.7:10: And my enemy will see and will be clothed with shame, she who says to me, "Where is the Lord your God?" My eyes will look upon her; now she will be trampled down like mud in the streets.
verses.7:11: On a day of plastering brick, that day is your blotting out, and that day will rub away your ordinances.
verses.7:12: And your cities will yield to leveling and to partitioning by the Assyrians, and your fortified cities to partitioning from Tyre to the river, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to the mountain.
verses.7:13: And the land will become a desolation together with those who dwell in it, because of the fruits of their practices.
verses.7:14: Shepherd Your people with Your rod, the sheep of Your inheritance, who dwell by themselves in a forest in the midst of Carmel; they will graze in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old.
verses.7:15: And according to the days of your departure from Egypt, you will see marvelous things.
verses.7:16: Nations will see and be ashamed even of all their strength; they will put hands over their mouth; their ears will become deaf.
verses.7:17: They will lick dust like a serpent, crawling on the ground; they will be thrown into confusion in their confinement. They will be astounded at the Lord our God, and they will be afraid of You.
verses.7:18: Who is a God like You, removing lawless deeds and passing over acts of ungodliness for the remnant of His inheritance? And He has not retained His wrath as a testimony, because He is one who desires mercy.
verses.7:19: He will return and have compassion on us; He will submerge our unrighteous deeds, and they will be cast away into the depths of the sea, all our sins.
verses.7:20: He will give in truth to Jacob, mercy to Abraham, just as You swore to our fathers in the former days.

notes.1:2: The Greek reads "words" (logous) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "all of you," and uses the doubled divine title kyrios Kyrios ("the Lord, the Lord").
notes.1:8: Unlike the Hebrew MT (first person, "jackals," "ostriches"), the Greek uses third-person feminine singular ("she") and renders the mourning creatures as "dragons" (drakonton) and "daughters of sirens" (thygateron seirenon).
notes.1:10: "Akim" (Greek Akeim) is a Septuagint-distinct proper name corresponding to the Hebrew wordplay on Acco/weeping, and "mockery from a house" renders a Greek common-noun reading where Hebrew MT has the place name Beth-le-aphrah.
notes.1:11: "Sennaar" (Greek Sennaar) is a Septuagint-distinct proper name corresponding to Zaanan in the Hebrew MT, while other place names in verses 11-15 are translated in Greek as common nouns.
notes.1:16: The Greek reads "your widowhood" (ten cherian sou) where the Hebrew MT has "your baldness."
notes.2:1: Unlike the Hebrew MT ("Woe to those... because it is in the power of their hand"), the Greek begins "They came to be" (Egenonto) and closes "because they did not lift up their hands to God."
notes.2:6: The Greek renders the Hebrew verb for "preach/drip" as "weep with tears" (klaiete dakrysin) and connects the end of verse 6 syntactically to "the one who says" (ho legon) in verse 7.
notes.2:8: The Greek reads "his peace" (tes eirenes autou) where the Hebrew MT has "garment," and "a crushing of war" (syntrimmon polemou) where MT has "those averse to war."
notes.2:9: The Greek reads "leaders of My people" (hegoumenoi laou mou) where the Hebrew MT has "women of My people," and concludes with the distinct command "Draw near to everlasting mountains."
notes.2:12: The Greek reads "in distress" (en thlipsei) where the Hebrew MT has "of Bozrah / in a fold," and "they will leap out" (exalountai) where MT describes the noise of a multitude.
notes.3:1: The Greek opens with third-person future "And he will say" (Kai erei) where the Hebrew MT has "And I said," and reads "remnant" (hoi kataloipoi) here and in 3:9 where MT has "rulers."
notes.3:7: The Greek expands "seers" to "those who see dreams," reads "will speak against them" where Hebrew MT has "will cover their mustache," and reads "no one who listens to them" where MT has "no answer from God."
notes.3:8: The Greek opens with the conditional "Unless" (ean me) and the active verb "I fill up strength" (empleso ischyn), contrasting elliptically with the false prophets of verses 6-7 (Hebrew MT: "On the other hand, I am filled with power").
notes.3:12: The Greek reads "fruit-watcher's hut" (oporophylakion, as in 1:6) where the Hebrew MT has "heaps of ruins," and "a forest grove" (alsos drymou) where MT has "high places of a forest."
notes.4:2: The Greek reads plural 'they will show us His way,' whereas the Hebrew text reads singular 'He will teach us of His ways.'
notes.4:8: Greek 'auchmodes' ('gloomy' or 'murky') reflects taking the Hebrew term for 'hill' (ophel) as 'darkness'; the Greek also reads 'from Babylon' where the Hebrew has the verb 'shall come.'
notes.4:13: The Greek reads 'you will melt down' (katatexeis) and 'you will dedicate their multitude' (to plethos auton), whereas the Hebrew reads 'you will crush' and 'I will devote their unjust gain.'
notes.4:14: The Greek reads 'the daughter will be hedged in with a hedge' and 'the gates (pylas) of Israel,' whereas other Greek manuscripts read 'the tribes (phylas) of Israel' and the Hebrew reads 'the judge of Israel.'
notes.5:1: The Greek text reads 'ex hou' ('from whom' or 'out of which'), whereas other Greek manuscripts and the Hebrew text read 'out of you.'
notes.5:3: In the Greek text, 'will see' (opsetai) stands alongside 'will shepherd,' and 'the Lord' (Kyrios) is nominative as the subject ('the Lord will shepherd') rather than genitive ('in the strength of the Lord') as in the Hebrew.
notes.5:4: Greek 'degmata anthropon' ('bites of men') reflects reading the Hebrew word for 'princes' (nesikei) as 'bites' (neshikei).
notes.5:6: The Greek reads 'like lambs (arnes) upon grass' and 'so that no one may be gathered together nor stand firm,' whereas the Hebrew reads 'like showers upon grass, which do not wait for man.'
notes.6:1: The Greek text reads 'Hear now a word. The Lord, the Lord (kyrios Kyrios) has said,' whereas other Greek manuscripts and the Hebrew text read 'Hear the word of the Lord; the Lord has said' or 'Hear what the Lord says.'
notes.6:5: Greek 'apo ton schoinon' ('from the reeds') renders the Hebrew place name Shittim as a common plant noun.
notes.6:8: The Greek opens with a passive question ('Has it been told to you') and renders the final clause 'to be ready to walk with the Lord your God,' whereas the Hebrew reads 'He has told you... to walk humbly with your God.'
notes.6:12: The Greek reads 'their tongue, be lifted up (hypsotheti) in their mouth,' using a second-person passive imperative; other Greek manuscripts read the indicative 'was lifted up,' and the Hebrew reads 'their tongue is deceitful.'
notes.6:16: The Greek preserves the distinct proper name Zambrei (Zimri) where the Hebrew text reads 'Omri'; the closing clause of 6:15 ('and the ordinances of My people will be wiped out') is also unique to the Greek.
notes.7:1: The Greek renders the harvest imagery as gathering straw (kalamēn) and takes "the first-grown fruits" (ta prōtogona) as the object of "to eat," closing with a second exclamation ("Woe to me, soul,") rather than the Hebrew "my soul desires the first-ripe fig."
notes.7:4: Continuing from v. 3b ("I will take away their goods"), the Greek portrays judgment as a moth eating away and walking on a measuring rod (kanonos) on a day of watching, diverging markedly from the Hebrew ("the best of them is like a brier").
notes.7:12: The Greek text reads eixousin ("will yield," from eikō) rather than hēxousin ("will come"), continuing v. 11's judgment oracle in which the cities are leveled and partitioned by the Assyrians, whereas the Hebrew promises people coming to Zion.
notes.7:18: The Greek reads "as a testimony" (eis martyrion) where the Hebrew has "forever" (lāʿad), reflecting a different vocalization of the same Hebrew consonants.
notes.7:20: The Greek text shifts from third person ("He will give," dōsei) to second person ("You swore," ōmosas) and reads dōsei eis alētheian ("He will give in truth"), whereas other Greek witnesses and the Hebrew read second-person "You will give truth" (dōseis alētheian).
